## Ahrefs vs Semrush: Which SEO Tool Should You Buy in 2026?


*Updated November 2026*


Buy Ahrefs if backlink research and clean, fast analysis drive your work. Buy Semrush if you want the bigger keyword database and a suite that also covers ads, social, and content tools. Both are excellent at measuring SEO. Neither does the SEO work for you, which is where most teams stall after the purchase.


This comparison covers the search intent behind "ahrefs vs semrush" and "semrush vs ahrefs" (same question, different word order), plus what to look at if you're searching for Ahrefs alternatives.

## Ahrefs vs Semrush at a glance


The table below uses vendor-published figures and rounded numbers. Index sizes and prices change often, so confirm anything you're about to pay for on each vendor's site.


Category Ahrefs Semrush


Entry paid plan Starter, $29/month at launch (verify current) Pro, $139.95/month list (verify current)


Free tier Ahrefs Webmaster Tools: free audits and backlink data for sites you verify Free account capped at roughly 10 requests per day and 10 tracked keywords


Backlink index claim Tens of trillions of links, from its own crawler Tens of trillions of links claimed


Keyword database Billions of keywords, broad country coverage Billions of keywords, 142 country databases


Rank tracking Rank Tracker, weekly updates by default, daily on demand Position Tracking, daily updates


AI visibility features Brand Radar (check plan and add-on pricing) AI Visibility Toolkit (check plan and add-on pricing)


Beyond SEO Light: some content and webmaster tools Heavy: ads research, social, content marketing, PR, local


A few rows deserve context. The free tiers aren't equivalent: Ahrefs gives you real data on your own site at no cost, while Semrush's free account works as a trial with a low daily ceiling. Index-size claims, meanwhile, are marketing numbers. Both vendors sit in the tens of trillions, and the useful question is how fresh and clean the data is for your niche.


## Where Ahrefs wins


Ahrefs wins on backlink data. It runs its own crawler, AhrefsBot, which is among the most active crawlers on the web, and that shows in how quickly new and lost links appear in Site Explorer. If you do link building, competitor link gap analysis, or digital PR reporting, this is the freshest view most practitioners can get without building their own tooling.


Three other strengths come up repeatedly in practitioner circles:


- **Interface speed.** Site Explorer, Keywords Explorer, and Content Explorer load fast and stay readable. Semrush has more modules, and navigating them takes longer.
- **Keyword metrics.** Ahrefs reports Keyword Difficulty based on the backlinks needed to rank, plus Traffic Potential, which estimates the total traffic the top page gets across all its keywords. Traffic Potential is a better prioritization input than raw volume for most content teams.
- **Webmaster Tools.** Free site audits and backlink monitoring on properties you own make Ahrefs the easiest paid tool to trial honestly.


The trade-off: Ahrefs has traditionally gone lighter on everything outside organic search. If your team also runs paid campaigns or social, you'll feel the gap. For plan tiers and what each unlocks, see our breakdown of[Ahrefs pricing](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/ahrefs-pricing) .


## Where Semrush wins


Semrush wins on breadth. Its keyword database spans 142 country databases, and the Keyword Magic Tool is the fastest way to turn one seed term into a few thousand grouped, filterable ideas. Add Topic Research, Content Marketing tooling, advertising research, and social tools, and you get one subscription that serves SEO, content, and paid teams at once.


Position Tracking updates daily, which matters when you're watching a migration or a core update play out. Semrush also ships its own AI visibility toolkit, so you can see how your brand shows up in AI-generated answers without bolting on another vendor. If you want a closer look at how the suite fits together, the[Semrush platform overview](https://www.sprites.ai/platform/semrush) covers the modules.


Its weaknesses are the mirror image of Ahrefs' strengths. Backlink analysis is good, but most link builders still reach for Ahrefs first. And the sheer module count means new users can spend a week figuring out which report to open.


[See the Semrush platform overview](https://www.sprites.ai/platform/semrush)


## Pricing as of November 2026


Both vendors price per seat tier with usage limits, and both change plans and add-ons often, so treat any number as a snapshot. The last list prices we verified: Ahrefs' Starter plan launched at $29 a month, and Semrush's Pro plan has listed at $139.95 a month. Anything above those entry tiers, and anything for AI visibility add-ons, should be checked on the vendor's pricing page today.


Entry price is a poor way to compare, though. The limit that bites first is different in each tool. On Ahrefs, it's usually report credits and tracked keywords at lower tiers. On Semrush, it's the cap on results per report and projects. Before you buy, list the three reports you'll run weekly, then check whether the plan you're eyeing covers them without hitting a ceiling.


Agencies feel this most. Seat counts and per-client project limits can double the real cost, so price the plan for your actual client count, not the headline tier.


## Semrush vs Ahrefs vs Moz vs Ubersuggest


If you're weighing four tools rather than two, here's how Moz and Ubersuggest fit.


Moz is the oldest brand in the group and the origin of Domain Authority, a metric many clients still ask about by name. Its keyword and link data are smaller than Ahrefs' or Semrush's, so it suits teams that want a simpler interface and reporting that clients already recognize.


Ubersuggest, from Neil Patel, is the budget option. It offers one-time purchase pricing in addition to subscriptions, which makes it attractive for solo site owners and small businesses. The data depth doesn't match the two leaders, and serious link analysis will outgrow it.


My view: for professional SEO work, the real decision is still Ahrefs or Semrush. Moz and Ubersuggest make sense when budget or simplicity outranks data depth.


## The gap both tools leave


Ahrefs and Semrush measure and recommend. They'll tell you that 40 pages have broken internal links, that a competitor ranks for 300 keywords you don't, and that your AI visibility dropped. Then the work lands on your team: brief the writer, draft the page, fix the redirects, add the schema, publish, and check back.


That handoff is where SEO programs slow down. The audit is done in an afternoon, and the fixes sit in a backlog for a quarter. In practice, the limiting factor for most teams is not data. It's execution capacity.


This is the case for SEO automation: an agent takes the finding and carries it through to a finished, publishable change. Every change waits for a human to approve it. You keep the judgment, and the agent does the labor.


Answer engine optimization raises the stakes. Getting cited in AI Overviews and chat answers requires structured, frequently updated pages, and that's a volume-and-maintenance problem more than a research problem.

"Best Ahrefs alternative" has no single answer, because teams leave Ahrefs for different reasons. Match the alternative to the gap you're actually feeling.

## Recommendation vs. human-approved execution


Pick the tool that matches the data you use every day. Choose Ahrefs for link work and fast, clean research. Choose Semrush for keyword breadth and a suite that serves more than SEO. Both will give you a prioritized list of what to fix.


The list is not the outcome, though. Rankings move when the fixes ship. A recommendation engine leaves that step to your calendar, while human-approved execution closes it: the agent drafts the change, you review it, and it goes live under your sign-off. Nothing publishes without you, and nothing waits in a backlog either.


If your reports already outrun your capacity to act on them, the next purchase probably isn't a third dashboard.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is Ahrefs better than Semrush?


It depends on the job. Ahrefs is stronger for backlink analysis and has a faster, cleaner interface. Semrush is stronger for keyword database size and for covering paid, social, and content work in the same subscription.


### Which is cheaper, Ahrefs or Semrush?


Ahrefs' entry plan has historically cost less, with Starter launching at $29 a month versus Semrush Pro's $139.95 list price. Both vendors change pricing often, so check current pricing before you decide. The cheaper plan isn't always cheaper in practice once usage limits and seat counts apply.


### What is the best Ahrefs alternative?


Semrush is the closest like-for-like replacement. Moz and Ubersuggest suit smaller budgets, and AI agents such as Sprites and Search Atlas suit teams that want the work executed rather than only measured. The best fit depends on whether your bottleneck is data or execution.


### How do Moz and Ubersuggest compare with Ahrefs and Semrush?


Moz and Ubersuggest have smaller data sets and fewer advanced features. Moz is known for Domain Authority and simple reporting, and Ubersuggest for low cost and one-time pricing. Both work for small sites, but professional link and competitor analysis usually points back to Ahrefs or Semrush.


### Do Ahrefs and Semrush track AI visibility?


Yes. Ahrefs offers Brand Radar and Semrush offers an AI Visibility Toolkit, and both show how your brand appears in AI-generated answers. Check each vendor's plan and add-on pricing, since availability varies by tier.


### Can Sprites replace Ahrefs or Semrush?


For many workflows, yes. Sprites handles keyword research, technical audits, backlink analysis, AI visibility tracking, content creation, and publishing, with human approval on every change. If link prospecting through a dedicated index is your daily task, you may keep Ahrefs or Semrush alongside it and let Sprites handle execution.
